title: MCP Server Production Deployment
description: Deploy MCP servers in production with Docker, Kubernetes, scaling policies, and observability hooks.

data.text: From Local MCP to Production Deployment

In development, MCP servers often run as local stdio processes. In production, they must be deployed as networked services with load balancing, auto-scaling, health checks, and observability. The transition from stdio to HTTP/SSE transport requires architectural changes: stateless sessions, connection pooling, and request-level tracing.

data.text: MCP servers can be containerized like any .NET application. Use multi-stage Docker builds to minimize image size, especially important since MCP servers may run on edge nodes or in constrained environments. The key is exposing the transport endpoint (HTTP/SSE) rather than stdio.

data.title: Dockerized MCP Server with HTTP Transport
data.content: Multi-stage Dockerfile and runtime configuration for production MCP servers:
data.code:
# Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY ["MyMcpServer.csproj", "."]
RUN dotnet restore "MyMcpServer.csproj"
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

# Install Node.js if the MCP server uses Node tools
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y nodejs npm

COPY --from=build /app/publish .

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1

EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyMcpServer.dll"]

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  mcp-server:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - MCP_TRANSPORT=http
      - MCP_PORT=8080
      - REDIS_CONNECTION=redis:6379
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - otel-collector
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '0.5'
          memory: 512M

data.text: In Kubernetes, deploy MCP servers as Deployments with HorizontalPodAutoscaler based on CPU or custom metrics (active sessions, pending tool calls). Use readiness gates to prevent routing traffic to pods still initializing the MCP transport layer.

data.title: Kubernetes Deployment with HPA
data.content: K8s YAML for MCP server with autoscaling and session-aware metrics:
data.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mcp-enterprise-nexus
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mcp-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mcp-server
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mcp-server
        image: mcp-enterprise-nexus:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        - name: MCP_TRANSPORT
          value: "http"
        - name: ASPNETCORE_URLS
          value: "http://+:8080"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "250m"
            memory: "256Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: mcp-server-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: mcp-enterprise-nexus
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70

data.text: In production, use HTTP/SSE transport instead of stdio. Stdio is designed for local development where each client spawns a new server process. At scale, this leads to resource exhaustion. HTTP transport allows connection pooling and shared server instances.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use HTTP/SSE transport for production — stdio is local-development only
Containerize with multi-stage builds and health checks
Deploy on Kubernetes with HPA based on CPU and session metrics
Use readiness gates to prevent routing to initializing pods
Instrument with OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing of MCP calls
data.takeaway: Production MCP deployment requires the full cloud-native stack — containerization, load balancing, autoscaling, health checks, and observability — applied to the MCP protocol's unique session and tool-calling model.
